tldr: Instead of waiting for real customers to find the breaking point, we built AI agents that call each other through the real voice stack and load test it on demand.
what: A load testing suite for a voice platform. Pairs of AI agents, one dialing and one receiving, place real calls through the full production pipeline: telephony, speech to text, the model, and text to speech, in both directions.
why: The only honest load is many real calls at once, and you cannot get that safely. Mocks, fake stand-ins for parts of the system, hide the failures that hurt, which live in the seams where the real pieces compete for resources.
how: Spin up many agent pairs with a set call count and rate limit, like crash test dummies driving a real car into a wall. The suite verified twenty concurrent calls end to end, the tested ceiling, not a theoretical maximum. It also caught that external and internal calls take different paths under load.
takeaway: Make the test real and the traffic fake. Break your system a hundred times with agents before a customer breaks it once.
